_readme: Declared corporate actions the vendor's split reference LACKS, read by the deep daily rebuild
(tools/history_lake/daily_build.py load_split_rows) beside ref/splits.json. Public corporate-action facts only:
date, ratio and evidence. No prices.
A row is refused unless evidence.capture names where it was read and evidence.price_verified is true: the vendor's
bars divided by the row's factor must reproduce an independent reference's closes on both sides of the date
(tests/test_history_lake_split_supplement.py).
A row the vendor later files itself (the same event within factors.SAME_EVENT_DAYS / SAME_EVENT_TOL) is not applied
twice; the vendor's wins.
NOT HERE, ON PURPOSE: CX 2008-05-06, listed by TradingView as 103:100, but its prices imply 1.0363 (with 103:100,
TradingView is still 0.608% lower on 2008-05-02 and 2008-05-05). Settle it from Cemex's 2008 recapitalization terms
before any row.
SPIN-OFFS (2026-11-21, Q-CLOSE-BASIS-3): the split table back-adjusts spin-offs too. Before this list the rebuild took
the second vendor's (Yahoo's) split-list ratio, admitted by the cliff test. TradingView's factor differs from it by up to
9% (FTI 2021). And F3b' (bars_sanitize._SPLIT_SIZE_TOL) declines a real spin-off whose event day also moved
(IRWD 2019, TRN 2018, T 2022), so a rebuild run would drop it.
PRINCIPLE: every TradingView-verified event the second vendor gets wrong, or the cliff test would decline, lives HERE;
the rebuild never leaves a verified event to the cliff test. daily_join.heal_splits treats a second-vendor event within
+-3 days of ANY table event as that event, whatever its ratio (tests/test_history_lake_daily_join.py).
NOT HERE, ON PURPOSE: ATRO 2018-10-10/11. TradingView does not back-adjust Astronics' Class-B distribution; the vendor's
1.15 on 10-11 stands (ruled). The second vendor's 1.182 on 10-10 is the same event and is no longer applied on top.
Verified within 0.05% of the second vendor's ratio and still admitted by the cliff test, so left on it: TKC 2004/2005,
MIDD 2026.
A row may name the vendor's own wrong figure for its event in replaces; merge drops exactly that vendor row (TKC 2006:
the vendor's 100:102.78 beside the second vendor's 1.1861; TradingView's step against the raw day files is 1.186057).
SEAM-61 (2026-11-21, Q-CLOSE-SEAM61): the 2003-09-10 seam batch. TradingView's request.splits lists splits and stock
dividends only (never a spin-off) and prints each ratio TRUNCATED to 3 decimals (1.5 as 1499:1000, 3% as 1029:1000), so
every size here is TradingView's step across the event against the vendor's RAW day files, from TradingView's own daily
closes; a listed split or stock dividend takes the exact fraction those closes pin within 0.001%.
73 adds/replaces: spin-offs, stock dividends and rights issues the vendor lacks or sizes differently. WY 2010:
TradingView lists 633:250, but its closes step exactly 5:2. VZ 2008-04-01 FairPoint: TradingView's own step is 0.980366,
the inverse of a spin-off; we match the reference (ruled).
27 DROP rows. Raw-continuous form: FLO 2003-11-25, CHY 2007-09-20 (TradingView takes no step and the
raw day files run straight through; applied, each drew a cliff that never traded). Small-event form (ruled): the vendor's
dividend-sized rows (within 5% of 1) that TradingView AND the second vendor both leave unadjusted:
NOT HERE, ON PURPOSE (held, stated): DB's 1.0582 TradingView step between 2003-09-10 and 2010-09-21 (not yet placed);
CASS (the vendor's raw prints differ from TradingView by up to 1% in Sep 2007: noise, not actions); KMB (no capture yet);
the identity-review six (DOC OKE TEVA CRH UMC RBCAA) and ITGR.
VNO 2017-07-18: TradingView 1.237391 against the second vendor's 1.237 (+0.032%): verified, admitted by the cliff test, left on it.
